items.subject: Compare one-stage and split weight-gradient reductions
items.objective: Own the weight-gradient kernel and its use of scratch in src/candidate.cu. Compare reduction granularities rather than assuming multi-stage partial sums win: test a CTA-level reduction distributed across B*L for each (h,j), and, where useful, split B*L into tiles that write partial sums to scratch followed by a final reduction. You may also test tiling neighboring j outputs if it enables useful reuse. Use no extra allocations; every scratch read must follow a write in the current call, and all outputs must be freshly written. Preserve bounds, the contracted gradient, full FP32, and the required tolerances for all valid inputs. Judge variants by correctness and complete-call timing, since the supplied baseline timing does not attribute cost to this kernel.
